request.system:
You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

Company (from SEC index): YOUGOV PLC
Form / document type: UK RNS / UK announcement: Final Results
Filed: 2026-10-13
Source URL: https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/80994acc-64b5-4b25-84b2-e915b675f09e.html

Document excerpt (paragraphs that mention staffing, restructuring, AI or automation):
<<<
Wide-reaching innovation, building a business for the AI world – accelerated efforts to enhance user interfaces, add new feature sets and introduce AI across our products.

YouGov Voices has already contributed to new business wins, including to a contract worth $2m, demonstrating early client demand for AI-enabled research solutions.

Progressed research automation, developing and testing workflows for lower-complexity projects to reduce manual effort, improve consistency and increase delivery scalability.

Research division saw improved performance with continued demand for strategic research projects, driven by expansion with financial services clients and rapid growth within the newly established AI sub-sector, partly offset by a strong prior-year comparator in election-related research.

“The broader macroeconomic focus on investment in AI infrastructure capable of delivering higher productivity underpins the growing importance of trusted data in an AI-driven world within the market research industry. This creates a significant opportunity for YouGov. I am delighted that Wayne Levings joins us next month as CEO-elect, to then step up to CEO and join the Board no later than February 2027. Following that, I will move into a non-executive role on the Board and will chair our newly formed Innovation Committee. I am confident that the actions we have taken to stabilise performance and strengthen the organisation mean that YouGov is well positioned to capitalise on the significant opportunities ahead.”

The macro-environment in which we operate in is changing faster than at any time in recent history. Technological advances mean that how we work has to evolve, what we work on is different and our offer to our customers needs to be reimagined. Understanding both the opportunity and the risks associated with AI goes to the heart of our strategic thinking.

Underpinning the business that Stephan has created at YouGov is an incredible asset, and that is our data. YouGov has unique proprietary data assets which we believe will play a crucial, and value-creating role in the AI-led transformation of our industry. It is the untapped value-creating potential in our data, especially in an AI world, which appealed when I was asked to join the Board last September and the quality of the asset reassured me when I stepped up to Chair in February.

The business will also need to continuously develop new products and enhance existing ones to continue to meet client needs. At the same time we need to look at all opportunities to embed efficiencies unlocked by AI throughout our business. We are addressing this in a systematic way in our Value Delivery Plan (VDP).

As well as the CEO role, we have to ensure we have the right skills and capabilities in the other positions around the boardroom. We need to ensure the Board understands the changing needs of our business, its strategy and the broader market context in which we operate. In practice, this means our Directors regularly meet with Stephan and the team above and beyond attending formal meetings. Recognising the complexity of the business, it also means we need a diverse mix of skills, capabilities and talent to deliver YouGov’s ambition. We have conducted an extensive review of the skills and experience we currently have in comparison to what we will need in the future to successfully support and challenge, in equal measure, the Executive team in the execution of our strategic objectives. As a result of this review, through rotation and succession planning, we anticipate appointing two Non-Executive Directors during FY27 to ensure orderly transition for the Audit & Risk Committee as Ashley Martin completes his nine-year term, and to further deepen our AI product and technology expertise. We will announce developments in our succession planning in due course.

I wish to take a moment to thank the Executive Leadership team and wider workforce on behalf of the Board for how they are embracing our transformation. Working in new ways accelerates cultural change and it is the Board’s role to ensure we uphold our values – be fast, be fearless, get it right, respect and trust – to preserve what makes YouGov unique while developing the new skills and capabilities to drive us forward. Stephan and the Board are confident in our direction of travel and believe this will transform the business, realise YouGov’s vision and deliver long-term value to stakeholders.

The past year has been characterised by continued macro-economic volatility and rapid advances in the implementation of Artificial Intelligence. Against a backdrop of geopolitical instability, organisations remained focussed on cost discipline. At the same time, investment increasingly shifted towards AI infrastructure capable of delivering higher productivity and returns. Within the market research industry, this has led to the growing importance of trusted data in an AI-driven world, creating a significant opportunity for YouGov.

Our ambition remains to become the universal infrastructure for trusted opinion and behavioural data sharing. We believe our proprietary panel, rich connected dataset and trusted brand place us in a unique position to help clients combine the power of AI with high-quality human data.

Our first priority was to stabilise performance by accelerating revenue growth and strengthening cost discipline. During the year, we maintained a measured approach to headcount expansion, refreshed the Leadership team, and concentrated investment on initiatives that support revenue generation, client value and long-term growth.

Having stabilised the business, our next focus was to increase momentum in product innovation to take advantage of the new opportunities presented by the rise of AI tools and capabilities. During FY26, we accelerated our efforts to enhance our user interfaces, add new feature sets and introduce AI across our products. In February 2026, we successfully launched YouGov Voices, an AI-powered interviewing tool enabling clients to collect rich, qualitative context from our panellists. As an add-on to YouGov BrandIndex, the product has helped secure several sales, including a $2m contract with a major professional services company. Early commercial success highlights growing demand for AI-enabled research solutions. In H2 FY26, we also introduced support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard across our products, enabling AI applications and agent environments to query our data using natural language.

Our focus on AI extends beyond product innovation and into the way we operate as a business. During the year, we made significant progress on our research automation programme, one of the largest transformation initiatives underway at YouGov. We developed and began testing automated workflows designed to streamline the delivery of low-complexity research projects, reducing manual effort while improving consistency and scalability. This work brings together advances in AI, data science and our platform capabilities, and represents an important step towards a more efficient operating model that will enable our teams to focus more of their time on delivering value to clients.

Our strategy goes beyond delivering leading market research and data analytics to our clients. It reflects a strategic shift towards embedding YouGov’s data directly into client workflows, platforms and AI-powered systems.

Over two decades, YouGov has built a strong foundation: a global proprietary panel, an automated data collection engine and a strong brand reputation. These competitive advantages are difficult to replicate and form the basis of our scalable, infrastructure-like model in this new age of AI.

AI-Powered Platform Transformation

Together, these initiatives represent important milestones in our evolution towards an AI-powered data and insights company, enabling us to deliver greater value to clients while accelerating innovation across the Group.

Looking ahead, we remain focussed on executing our strategy and delivering the full benefits of the transformation programme underway across the business. We are combining proprietary data assets, advanced analytics capabilities and emerging AI technologies. Together, these capabilities position YouGov to provide faster, richer and more actionable data at scale.

As announced earlier this year, the Company has launched a VDP which comprises three waves. The waves combine efficiency improvements and enhanced ways of working along with significant transformation enabled by AI. Plus, wave 3 also includes new revenue streams.

Wave 1, completed in March 2026, delivered an annualised £2.5m reduction in the cost base through targeted headcount and other cost reductions in non-revenue-generating areas. H2 26 includes some benefit for this action already. FY27 will benefit from the full year impact.

Wave 3 will focus on opening up new revenue streams through development of AI-powered products and our Data-as-a-Product capabilities. Our product development, data science and technology teams continue to make strides on these initiatives, including introducing imputation to our dataset and developing newer products such as YouGov Parallax.

Data Products delivered revenue growth of 2% on a reported basis and 3% in underlying terms1. Growth was driven by our key US market, on the back of new client wins across several sectors. Continued investment in our subscription-based products to enhance the user experience and introduce AI-enabled capabilities also helped maintain stable renewal rates in the period. The division’s return to growth, despite continued pressure on client budgets, is testament to the quality and relevance of our products and we are encouraged by early commercial interest in new and upcoming product launches.

The key cash item within SRI in both years is restructuring and integration costs. The restructuring and integration cost category is a key area of focus within the business and once the VDP is complete, we would expect this aspect to be immaterial. However, as the VDP gains deep momentum throughout FY27, this will continue to be a material number in the short term.

The items considered as separately reportable are acquisition or divestment related costs, material re organisation, restructuring and integration costs, large-scale technological transformation programmes, amortisation of acquired customer list and order backlog intangibles, impairment charges and other material incremental non-recurring items.

In preparing the financial statements for the current year, Management has identified an error in the income tax calculations for the prior year, relating to the tax treatment of the step up in the tax base on goodwill in Germany following the pre-restructuring steps undertaken by GfK prior to YouGov’s acquisition of Shopper. To correct this, the income tax charge for the prior year has been reduced by £2.7m, with a corresponding increase to current tax assets. This adjustment is non-cash, and does not affect the statement of cash flows.

Restructuring and integration costs

The impairment charges on intangible assets and right-of-use assets, and restructuring and integration costs recognised in the current year, relate to the Value Delivery Plan, first announced alongside the Group’s half-year results (see the update on Value Delivery Plan section in the Chief Financial Officer’s Review for more information). The intangible assets impaired support certain non-core products which will be discontinued in 2027. The right-of-use assets impaired are three underutilised offices. The restructuring and integration costs primarily consist of redundancy payments, consultancy fees, and other legal and professional fees.
>>>
